critical.finding: The model's FY2026 starting revenue is stale and about 15% too low, so every scenario price (fair value, the yearly table, what_must_be_true) rests on a wrong base. The revenue_current_fy assumption takes FY2025 revenue (NT$3,809bn, labelled 'ttm') x 1.253 = NT$4,771bn for FY2026. The run's own reported quarters say otherwise: Q1 1,134.1 + Q2 1,270.4 + Q3 1,494.2 = NT$3,898.7bn for 9M 2026 (nm_revenue_q1_2026, nm_revenue_q2_2026, nm_revenue_q3_2026). The real TTM is NT$4,944.8bn (with nm_revenue_q4_2025). FY2026 at the Q4 guide midpoint (US$53.3bn x 31.8 NT$, dc release/call) is about NT$5,590bn (+47%). The Nov-Dec stub carries NT$861bn, while two thirds of the Q4 guide is about NT$1,130bn. Result: the base's 'growth >25% in 2027' is only about +8% on the real FY2026 (model FY2027 NT$6,055bn vs ~5,590bn). Base FY2027 operating EPS of NT$99 is below the Q3 2026 run rate (EPS 29.43 x 4 = ~118, quarter_result). Base FY2028 EPS 118.6 equals today's run rate. The bear 'growth 6%' is really about -10% in 2027 and -8% in 2028 against the real base. The narratives in position/core.json and coherence.md describe a different business than the one priced.
